decision: SoD enforcement is an additive 'step 3.6' inside the one resolveFor decision core, active iff op in {approve, transition} AND an optional injected deps.sod port is present (the exact structural analogue of T-0034's invoke-path step 3.5 behind deps.effects). The SoD decision logic lives in a new pure module src/core/sod.ts (static/dynamic decision functions + the SodSource constraint-loading port), imported by grant-resolver.ts as effect-resource.ts is. Static SoD is a query over EFFECTIVE role_assignment rows; dynamic SoD is recomputed from the actor_event ledger at action-time (attribution = COALESCE(on_behalf_of, actor)); no new derived state. On a guarded op that passes covering-grant AND SoD AND record-fetch, the gateway appends exactly one actor_event row via the injected T-0019 ActorEventWriter (implemented now over an in-memory store; Postgres DAO is T-0053); on any denial (no_grant / sod_violation / not_found) zero rows are written. A violation returns { denied: true, reason: 'sod_violation' } (fail-closed). The new sod_constraint table (migration 027) is a T-0013 tenant table; the FO-T0019-1 forward debt is closed by a BEFORE UPDATE no-decrement trigger on actor_event_seq (migration 028). The SoD-read + actor_event-write on a guarded op are ONE transaction, bound to the same withTenant PoolClient at the T-0053 DAO layer (pinned as fitness obligation FF-SOD8); in static-now the testable surrogate is exactly-one-row-on-pass / zero-on-deny.

rejected_alternatives.option: Separate SoD authorization module (a la T-0029 scoped-admin) invoked around resolveFor
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Breaks the single-chokepoint invariant (NF-5) and creates a second action-time authority path that can diverge from the covering-grant decision. T-0029 is legitimately separate because it pre-filters which management ops a scoped admin may attempt (a different axis); SoD is inherently an action-time query over the per-object ledger at the transition instant, so it belongs at the same gateway step where the covering grant is decided. Step 3.6 keeps ONE decision core.

rejected_alternatives.option: A derived approval_state / SoD-decision-cache table updated on each transition
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A second source of truth that can drift from the ledger and reintroduces the read-modify-write the ledger was built to avoid. SoD is recomputable from actor_event + role_assignment at action-time (TOCTOU-safe like the grant check). Spec section 3.2/6 forbid it.

rejected_alternatives.option: Software-only no-decrement guard validating next_seq monotonicity in the TS writer
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Defeatable by any other caller and invisible to CI. The structural fix (a BEFORE UPDATE trigger on actor_event_seq) is always-on, role-agnostic (rejects even the owner), and requires a CI-visible DDL diff to defeat (spec section 3.4 option A, the preferred fix).

rejected_alternatives.option: Make deps.sod a required field on ResolverDeps
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A breaking change to every existing caller and to the frozen-test import surface (NF-6, FE-W23-0008). Must be optional, mirroring deps.effects / deps.classifications.

rejected_alternatives.option: Encode static-SoD as a DB CHECK / EXCLUDE constraint on role_assignment
rejected_alternatives.why_not: That is the assignment-time block (E4.6 / T-0039), explicitly out of scope. T-0032 enforces SoD only on the action-time approve/transition path plus ships the standalone query (FR-10). A DB constraint would also edit a frozen table's write-path.

rejected_alternatives.option: Single migration 027 holding both the sod_constraint table and the seq trigger
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Permitted by spec (section 3.5 'MAY collapse') but kept as two files (027 table, 028 trigger) because the trigger targets a different table (actor_event_seq, T-0019's) than the new sod_constraint; cleaner separation. Either is acceptable; the run-seam requirement is only >=027, lexicographically after 022.

contracts: resolveFor(deps, handle, subject, op, invokeCtx?, guardCtx?): Promise<ResolvedView | EffectDeniedView | SodDeniedView> — additive optional guardCtx 6th arg (mirrors invokeCtx); guarded op with deps.sod present but guardCtx absent => fail-closed sod_violation (NF-3, unattributable transition cannot be proven SoD-clean)

Step 3.6 (inside resolveFor, after step 3.5, before record-fetch): if op in {approve,transition} AND deps.sod present => evaluateSod; on violated or any thrown port error => return { denied:true, reason:'sod_violation' } (zero actor_event rows). Absent deps.sod => step skipped (pre-T-0032 behavior, NF-2).
Step 6.5 (inside resolveFor, after record-fetch, on PASS of a guarded op): deps.sod.writer.appendActorEvent(toActorEventInput(act)) appends EXACTLY ONE row (AC-10).

detectStaticConflict(assignments, constraints, ancestry): SodDecision — pure; same principal holds role_a AND role_b with both org_scopes intersecting the constraint scope (AncestryOracle, no new scope algebra).
wouldCreateStaticConflict(existing, candidate, constraints, ancestry): SodDecision — FR-10 standalone assignment-conflict query.

evaluateDynamicSod(reader, constraints, act): Promise<SodDecision> — DSoD-1 self-approval block (didPrincipalPerform(ref,'submit',P)); DSoD-2 approve_L1 != L2; attribution COALESCE(onBehalfOf, actor) via actorEventPrincipal.
evaluateSod(source, ancestry, act, principalAssignments): Promise<SodDecision> — top-level guard combining static + dynamic; fail-closed on any port error.
